subsystems.name: Actuation system
subsystems.role: produces the high torque and precise motion needed to stand, walk and lift.

subsystems.name: Proprioceptive sensing
subsystems.role: gives the robot an internal sense of joint angles, forces and body orientation.
parts: force-torque sensors at wrists and ankles

subsystems.name: Tactile skin
subsystems.role: detects contact, pressure and slip on hands, fingers and body surfaces.

subsystems.name: Control and compute
subsystems.role: runs balance, gait and manipulation algorithms in a hard real-time loop.

subsystems.name: Power
subsystems.role: supplies energy to actuators and electronics for a useful working period.

subsystems.name: Structure and end-effectors
subsystems.role: provides a lightweight frame and dexterous hands that can grasp varied objects.

buildSteps.title: Define the kinematic design
buildSteps.detail: Choose the number of joints, limb lengths and payload so the robot can reach and lift what the job requires.

buildSteps.title: Build joint modules
buildSteps.detail: Integrate motors, gearboxes and torque sensors into compact actuator units that fit inside each limb.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the skeleton
buildSteps.detail: Connect the joint modules with lightweight links to form a humanoid torso, arms and legs.

buildSteps.title: Integrate sensors
buildSteps.detail: Mount IMUs on the torso and limbs, fit joint encoders, and cover hands and body with tactile skin.

buildSteps.title: Write the control software
buildSteps.detail: Develop whole-body control that uses proprioceptive feedback to keep balance, walk and manipulate objects.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Identify sensor offsets, actuator friction and dynamics, then tune controllers so the robot moves smoothly.

buildSteps.title: Test in simulation and on hardware
buildSteps.detail: Start with standing and balancing, progress to walking, then to reaching and grasping.

buildSteps.title: Validate in pilot tasks
buildSteps.detail: Run the robot in a real workspace, such as moving boxes or tending a machine, and measure reliability.

prerequisites.why: human-scale strength is needed without making the robot too heavy to balance.
balance and contact tasks require control loops running at around 1 kHz.
durable, high-resolution skin that covers curved, moving surfaces is still maturing.
current lithium-ion packs give only a limited runtime under heavy load.
training control policies in simulation speeds up development but transfer to the real world remains imperfect.

pathway.milestone: humanoids performing structured tasks in logistics and manufacturing pilots
pathway.unlocks: evidence that balance and basic manipulation are reliable enough for paid work.

pathway.milestone: dexterous manipulation of varied objects without custom fixtures
pathway.unlocks: tasks such as kitting, machine tending and simple assembly.

pathway.milestone: robust autonomy in unstructured human spaces
pathway.unlocks: general labor in factories, construction sites and homes.
widespread deployment as a general-purpose workforce.
